subject: English Language

questions.prompt: Which subject was the teacher teaching? (A Kiswahili, B English, C science, D mathematics)
steps: The included page 1 listening passage names English.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator remember? (A teacher, B self-introduction, C best moment at a new school, D class)
steps: This is the passage's opening topic.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. The best moment at a new school.

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator feel afraid? (A all pupils looked at the narrator, B introducing in English, C first entry, D overcoming fear)
steps: The passage explicitly gives this cause.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Everyone turned their eyes on the narrator.

questions.prompt: What did the teacher ask the narrator to do? (A sit, B cheer, C teach, D introduce in English)
steps: The teacher's instruction is stated directly.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Why did the class cheer? (A happy, B good English, C overcame fear, D first arrival)
steps: The successful effort immediately precedes the cheering.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. The narrator overcame fear and introduced himself/herself.

questions.prompt: Bring the letter ___ the postman left. (A who, B whose, C which, D whom)
steps: Which refers to the letter.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Children prefer playing ___ eating. (A and, B to, C both, D with)
steps: Use prefer X to Y.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I will see a doctor ___ I do not feel better. (A if, B although, C unless, D yet)
steps: If introduces the condition for the visit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Report Yohana said, I feel dizzy.
steps: Change I to he and backshift feel to felt in ordinary past reporting.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Yohana said that he felt dizzy.

questions.prompt: ___ the visitors arrived, we welcomed them. (A as, B while, C when, D was)
steps: When introduces the arrival event.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. When (intended); A. as is also possible.

questions.prompt: Which is a compound word? (A butterflies, B beautiful, C difficult, D company)
steps: Butterfly is built from butter and fly; butterflies is its plural.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I ___ English for ten weeks now. (A has been learning, B have been learn, C have been learning, D had learnt)
steps: I takes have; been learning describes an activity continuing until now.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where is the boy ___ you were speaking to? (A whose, B who, C which, D whom)
steps: The pronoun is the object of speaking to.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. Whom (formal object); B. who is accepted in ordinary English.

questions.prompt: I looked at ___ in the mirror. (A self, B my face, C myself, D ourself)
steps: Use myself when the object is the speaker as a whole.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Myself (intended reflexive); B. my face is also meaningful.

questions.prompt: The news ___ broadcast on television. (A is, B are, C were, D will)
steps: News is grammatically singular.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Anna always ___ her husband on Saturday. (A visiting, B visited, C visitinling, D visits)
steps: A singular subject takes visits for a current habit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: If they ___ enough training, they would have won. (A have, B had, C would had, D would have)
steps: The complete past-perfect condition needs had had; the first had is auxiliary and the second means received.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Had is the best printed choice. For a past unreal condition: If they had had enough training, they would have won.

questions.prompt: If it rain we ___ not going to school. (A shall, B should)
steps: Shall/should require a base verb or be; neither can directly precede not going here.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: No correct completion as printed. Correct future: If it rains, we shall not go to school. Correct continuous: If it rains, we are not going to school.

questions.prompt: What is a thug? (A violent person, B dirty person, C beautiful person, D ugly person)
steps: Thug refers to a violent criminal or aggressive person.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: They have learned English ___ six years. (A for, B after, C since, D before)
steps: For introduces duration.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Our teacher has been sick ___ last month. (A after, B before, C since, D for)
steps: Since introduces the starting time.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Children were tired ___ they still wanted to play. (A and, B also, C yet, D but)
steps: Tiredness and continued desire to play contrast.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. But or C. yet express the intended contrast; A. and also links the statements grammatically.

questions.prompt: Opposite of beautiful? (A good, B small, C handsome, D ugly)
steps: Ugly is the usual opposite of beautiful.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Make passive: The man brought pens.
steps: Move pens to the subject and use were brought to keep past tense.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Pens were brought by the man.

questions.prompt: Juma's behaviour differs ___ his father's. (A from, B with, C than, D to)
steps: Different from is the expected comparison phrase.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Make I love my country plural. (A I loved my country, B we love our country, C we loved our country, D she loved the country)
steps: Change I to we and my to our while retaining present tense.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: We are going to school, ___? (A don't we, B are we, C aren't we, D did we)
steps: A positive are statement takes a negative are tag.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Your work is ___ than yesterday. (A worse, B bad, C worst, D worses)
steps: Worse is the irregular comparative of bad.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Henish ___ to school ___ foot daily. (A goes/on, B go/on, C goes/by, D goes/with)
steps: A singular habitual subject takes goes; walking is on foot.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who flies an aeroplane? (A doctor, B pilot, C captain, D soldier)
steps: A pilot operates an aircraft.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: A young elephant is a ___. (A cab, B cow, C fawn, D calf)
steps: Calf is the young-elephant term.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Mambo has been headteacher ___ 1980. (A for, B since, C if, D on)
steps: Since introduces the starting year.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Mwaija got good test marks. She is ___. (A coward, B intelligent, C beautiful, D powerful)
steps: The context associates good academic performance with intelligence.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Your brother's son is your ___. (A uncle, B cousin, C nephew, D niece)
steps: Nephew is the male child of one's sibling.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: It is found in Iringa region, Tanzania.
steps: Location follows introduction of Ruaha National Park.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: It has five big animals like elephant, rhino, giraffe and lion.
steps: Animal examples follow the park's introduction, location and size. The printed list contains four examples despite saying five.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Many tourists visit to see Ruaha's beauty.
steps: The visitors sentence concludes the description.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Ruaha is the second-largest park in Tanzania.
steps: Name the park before sentences beginning It.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: It has about 22893 kilometres (printed).
steps: Place the size after location. Area should be in square kilometres; the printed figure is not the TANAPA figure.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is Mr. Macha's job?
steps: The first sentence gives his occupation.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which child is the bank clerk?
steps: The passage names this child as the bank clerk.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does the farmer in the passage do?
steps: The second-born child's work is stated explicitly.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does the doctor do?
steps: The passage directly describes the first-born child's job.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does a policewoman do?
steps: The passage gives the occupation but not its duties; this is the appropriate general description.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Maintains law and order, helps protect people and investigates crime.

summaries.Listening and grammar: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Grammar and composition: Follow a clear sequence and keep the tense consistent. Introduce people and events before their pronouns, actions and final outcome.
summaries.Comprehension: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: Standard Six Exams | 2010 - 2023 | Monthly, Midterm, Terminal and Annual Exams - Download All Subjects - Msomi Bora

limitations: Numbering: 23 is absent in the printed paper, so 44 tasks are covered.
17: Fully past unreal condition requires had had, absent from the choices.
18: Neither auxiliary fits the printed verb phrase; both corrected versions are supplied.
37,40: Animal list count and area wording are defective. TANAPA lists Ruaha at about 20,226 square kilometres, rather than the printed figure.
